instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor conducting a reassessment. Analyse the prior assessment summary, changes since last assessment, and updated survey, then respond with a complete reassessment JSON including score_delta, carry_forward, progress, and comparison_to_previous.

answers.companyDescription: Asset management firm managing €2.5B AUM across 6 mutual funds and discretionary mandates for institutional investors and family offices. Investment strategies span European equities, fixed income, and multi-asset. Evaluating machine learning overlays for portfolio risk monitoring and alternative data integration for equity research. A tight-knit operation where everyone wears multiple hats. We have no dedicated innovation budget — improvements happen opportunistically when the team identifies a clear bottleneck affecting our core operations or customer experience.
answers.pastInitiatives: We installed IoT sensors on 40% of our production equipment to monitor utilization and predict failures. The pilot showed a 15% reduction in unplanned downtime on instrumented machines. We now have a business case approved for full fleet rollout, but procurement and integration with our legacy maintenance system are proving more complex than anticipated.
answers.strategicGoals: Customer retention has declined from 92% to 84% over the past 18 months, primarily among our mid-tier and enterprise segments. Exit interviews consistently cite product stagnation and poor digital self-service tools as reasons for leaving. We need to urgently modernize our customer-facing technology and proactively address the specific pain points driving churn before the trend becomes irreversible.
answers.teamSize: We have 2 generalist developers who split their time between maintaining our existing systems, handling customer support escalations, and occasionally prototyping new features. There is no dedicated innovation or R&D role — innovation happens when these developers have spare cycles between urgent operational tasks, which is rare.

input.changes_since_last: Product launch successful — 4 new features shipped. Customer NPS improved 20 points. Backlog of technical debt growing.

opportunities.title: Phased Digital Customer Experience Overhaul
opportunities.rationale: Declining customer retention (92% to 84%) is directly tied to product stagnation and poor digital self-service. This opportunity focuses on strategically improving key customer touchpoints, leveraging the recent product success without requiring a massive, immediate overhaul.

first_actions: Conduct deep dive UX research focusing specifically on mid-tier/enterprise pain points cited in exit interviews.
Scope the modernization effort to one high-impact, low-complexity area (e.g., document upload or basic statement retrieval) for a quick win MVP.
Build a business case mapping specific improvements directly to measurable retention uplift rates.
execution_plan.success_metric: Reduction in customer service inquiries related to self-service tasks by 20% within 6 months.
milestones: Completion of pain point mapping and user journey diagrams (Month 1)
MVP development and internal QA sign-off (Month 3)
Pilot launch with a specific segment of mid-tier clients (Month 4)

opportunities.title: Technical Debt Governance and Capacity Planning
opportunities.rationale: The growing backlog of technical debt is consuming the limited time of generalist developers, creating an operational drag. Formalizing a process to allocate dedicated capacity for maintenance prevents future bottlenecks and frees resources necessary for digital improvements.

first_actions: Perform a rapid audit of the top 5 most frequently failing or resource-intensive areas of code/system.
Implement a 'Debt Sprint' cycle (20% capacity) into the next development sprint to address critical refactoring tasks.
Establish clear ownership roles for system components to reduce generalist reliance.
execution_plan.success_metric: Reduction in critical bugs reported by 30% quarter-over-quarter.
milestones: Completion of initial code audit and risk matrix (Month 1)
Successful execution of first dedicated 'Debt Sprint' (Month 2)
Measurable decrease in Mean Time To Resolution (MTTR) for critical incidents (Ongoing)

next_steps.action: Formalize a recurring 'Discovery & Pain Point Quantification' session with sales/account teams to validate the highest leverage customer pain points identified in exit interviews.
Allocate and ring-fence a dedicated minimum of 10% developer capacity for technical debt management, reporting usage weekly.
Draft a preliminary 'Minimum Viable Digital Feature' scope document based on the prioritized pain point, defining measurable success criteria.

key_weaknesses: Lack of dedicated R&D or Innovation role significantly constrains proactive development capacity.
High reliance on generalist talent, leading to context switching and technical debt accumulation.
Strategy remains reactive; the urgency of digital modernization is outpacing strategic planning ability.

improvements: Successful product feature launch (4 new features) increased immediate operational value.
NPS improved by 20 points, indicating better short-term customer satisfaction.
persistent_gaps: Core digital self-service gaps persist and are actively contributing to major churn risks.
Technical debt is growing faster than it can be addressed due to resource strain.
Internal process maturity remains 'partial', hindering systematic improvement across departments.
achieved_milestones: Successful deployment of four new features (Product increment).
Completed the critical steps outlined in prior recommendations regarding IoT sensors/operations.

comparison_to_previous.key_changes: The focus has shifted from operational efficiency (IoT/Technical Debt) to critical market defense (Customer Churn). While operational success was achieved recently (NPS rise), the core strategic threat—customer digital experience stagnation—has escalated and becomes the immediate priority.
